items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: And I had a teacher who would show me what chord changes were and how to write things out

ctx.x: The other question I had was composing your own music is obviously very important to you. Did you have a time, can you remember the first time you wrote your own tune?

I was very young. I started studying piano, I think I was about four or five, four. And unlike other kind of classical early piano study, I began early on improvising and not knowing it. And I had a teacher who would show me what chord changes were and how to write things out, so that even when I was beginning to study the piano, I was also improvising at the same time. I didn’t know it. So my learning process went hand in hand, you know, improvising and studying written form as well. So it was not like it was…
It’s fortunate that you had a piano teacher that could give you a little support in that area.
